concept: Instructions files, skills, subagents, hooks, MCP servers, and plugins differ in when they load, what they cost, who triggers them, and whether they are guaranteed to run.
source_note: Text follows Module 5's comparison table, decision chart, and design exercise. Token costs are from the module's measured install of its example plugin.
rules_of_thumb: If it must happen every time, it's a hook (or a permission rule), not an instruction or a skill. Only the harness can guarantee an action; the model can only be asked.
If it's needed sometimes, it's a skill, not part of the instructions file: pay for the description always, the body only when it's used.

mechanisms.label: Instructions file
mechanisms.deterministic: No: the model may ignore it.

mechanisms.label: Skill
mechanisms.what: A folder with SKILL.md, plus optional scripts and reference files.
mechanisms.loads: Short description on every request; full body only when used. Measured: about 80 tokens always, 190 more when it runs.
mechanisms.triggered: The model (matching the description) or the user (by name).
mechanisms.deterministic: The instructions aren't; its scripts are, once run.
mechanisms.runs_code: Yes, through the agent's normal tools and permissions.

mechanisms.label: Subagent
mechanisms.what: A separate agent with its own system prompt, tools, and context.
mechanisms.loads: Its own requests; only its final summary returns to the main conversation. Measured: about 40 tokens always, 130 when invoked.
mechanisms.triggered: The model delegates, or the user asks.
mechanisms.runs_code: Only through the tools it's allowed.

mechanisms.label: Hook
mechanisms.what: Your script, run by the harness at a lifecycle event (before a tool call, after an edit, at session start).
mechanisms.loads: None, unless its output is injected into context. Measured: no context cost.
mechanisms.triggered: The harness, every time the event fires.
mechanisms.runs_code: Yes, as you, outside any sandbox.

mechanisms.label: MCP server
mechanisms.what: A process or service that offers tools over the Model Context Protocol.
mechanisms.loads: Tool names and descriptions on requests (some harnesses defer full definitions); results when called.
mechanisms.deterministic: The server's code is; the model's choice to call it isn't.
mechanisms.runs_code: Yes, with the server's own access.

mechanisms.label: CLI tool
mechanisms.what: An existing command (git, psql, an internal CLI).
mechanisms.runs_code: Yes, as you, inside the sandbox if one is on.

mechanisms.label: Plugin
mechanisms.what: A packaged, versioned set of skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers.
mechanisms.loads: The sum of its components, in every session where it's enabled.
mechanisms.triggered: Installed by a user or an administrator.

attributes.label: When it loads, and context cost

nodes.label: Must it happen every time?
nodes.text: Must it happen every time, regardless of what the model decides?

nodes.label: Access to an external system?
nodes.text: Is it access to an external system or data?

nodes.label: Does a good CLI exist?
nodes.text: Does a good command-line tool already exist for it?

nodes.label: Relevant to nearly every task?
nodes.text: Is it a fact or constraint relevant to nearly every task?

nodes.label: Lots of output, or unbiased view?
nodes.text: Does it produce lots of output, or need an unbiased view?

nodes.label: Hook or permission rule
nodes.why: Only the harness can guarantee an action; the model can only be asked.

nodes.label: Use the CLI
nodes.why: Document the command in the instructions file or a skill. The CLI costs nothing until used and runs under the permission rules and sandbox you already have.

nodes.label: MCP server
nodes.why: An external system with no CLI: the server can hold the credentials and limit what the agent can do.

nodes.label: Instructions file
nodes.why: A short fact relevant to nearly every task belongs where it is always present.

nodes.label: Subagent
nodes.why: Its own context keeps verbose work out of yours, and a fresh context gives an unbiased view.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.why: Needed sometimes: pay for the description always, the body only when it is used.

share_yes.label: Package as a plugin
share_yes.why: A versioned bundle everyone installs from an internal marketplace. Disable plugins you are not using: every enabled component costs context in every session.

scenarios.text: Run the code formatter after every file edit.
scenarios.explanation: Hook (after edits): it must happen every time.

scenarios.text: Teach the agent your team's six-step release procedure, used about once a month.
scenarios.explanation: Skill: needed occasionally; the description costs little until it's used.

scenarios.text: Let the agent look up tickets in your internal issue tracker, which has an API but no CLI.
scenarios.explanation: MCP server: an external system with no CLI; the server can hold the credentials and limit what the agent can do.

scenarios.text: Never allow a commit directly to main.
scenarios.explanation: Hook or permission rule, backed by branch protection on the git server: a harness control stops the agent; server-side protection stops everyone.

scenarios.text: Get an independent review of a large diff without the bias of the session that wrote it.
scenarios.explanation: Subagent with read-only tools: a fresh context and least privilege.

scenarios.text: Give every developer the same skills, hooks, and servers, and update them centrally.
The test command is make test, not pytest.
scenarios.explanation: Instructions file: a short fact relevant to nearly every task.

takeaway: Put facts in the instructions file, procedures in skills, guarantees in hooks, systems behind MCP, and bundles in plugins. Every one of them except the first runs code as you.
